alt: A two-row table comparing the correct chain of at-most comparisons with a chain that uses strictly-less-than. On a cost that sits exactly on a boundary the two versions print different tiers, while on a cost away from a boundary they agree and hide the mistake.

steps.caption: The cost is 20. Two versions of the same chain differ only in the comparison: <= against <.
With <=, the first check is 20 <= 20 and the second is 20 <= 50. The program prints Standard, which is what the problem asks.
With <, 20 is not below the boundary, so it falls through to the next branch and the program prints Priority. That is wrong, and only a test on the boundary shows it.
The cost is 50. Two versions of the same chain differ only in the comparison: <= against <.
With <=, the first check is 50 <= 20 and the second is 50 <= 50. The program prints Priority, which is what the problem asks.
With <, 50 is not below the boundary, so it falls through to the next branch and the program prints Express. That is wrong, and only a test on the boundary shows it.
The cost is 18. Two versions of the same chain differ only in the comparison: <= against <.
With <=, the first check is 18 <= 20 and the second is 18 <= 50. The program prints Standard, which is what the problem asks.
With <, the answer is also Standard. This cost sits away from a boundary, so the wrong comparison hides and this test would not catch it.
